sections.content: How many people are "prison service officers (below principal officer)"?

37,245 people

were counted on the census as "prison service officers (below principal officer)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Prison service officers (below principal officer) direct, co-ordinate and participate in guarding inmates and maintaining discipline in prisons and other detention centres.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "prison service officers (below principal officer)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "prison service officers (below principal officer)", 15.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "prison service officers (below principal officer)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "prison service officers (below principal officer)" included:

  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers
  • assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "prison service officers (below principal officer)" there were more men than women (64.4% compared with 35.6%).

This means "prison service officers (below principal officer)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "protective service occupations".

Men made up 64.4% and women made up 35.6% of "prison service officers (below principal officer)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "prison service officers (below principal officer)" included:

  • IT quality and testing professionals
  • chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants
  • web design professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "prison service officers (below principal officer)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "prison service officers (below principal officer)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "prison service officers (below principal officer)", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90.5% compared with 9.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.4%) than self-employed (0.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included County Durham, this is in the region of the North East.
